business_patterns.top_pattern: IN DSNP HMO spend is trapped in a massive Not Mapped bucket
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: IN DSNP HMO / Not Mapped facility bucket
business_patterns.pattern_details: IN DSNP HMO spend is heavily concentrated in a Not Mapped facility bucket, adding about $66.0M. Claim volume also increased materially, but because the facility classification is missing, it is not possible to tell whether the change reflects true utilization growth, a site-of-care shift, or a mapping problem. This should be treated as a gating validation issue before broader authorization, reimbursement, or network actions are taken in IN DSNP HMO.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A misclassified bucket this large can distort every downstream conclusion about provider mix, site of care, and utilization management performance.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Validate and reclassify the IN DSNP HMO Not Mapped claims at the facility and product level, then rerun authorization, reimbursement, and provider analyses only after the mapping issue is resolved.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The increase sits in a Not Mapped facility bucket and is explicitly flagged as unmapped or unknown, so business action should wait for classification cleanup.
evidence_summary: IN DSNP HMO in the Not Mapped facility bucket added about +$66.0M.
Claim count increased by 123,376, with unit cost indicators also moving up.
This single bucket represents about 80% of the positive delta in its evidence set.
The contributing group carries an unmapped or unknown value flag.

business_patterns.top_pattern: UNATTRIBUTED outpatient temporary-code spend needs validation before action
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: UNATTRIBUTED outpatient ancillary and management categories
business_patterns.pattern_details: UNATTRIBUTED outpatient spend rose sharply in OP HH/DME and OP Mgmt Oth Misc, concentrated in Not Mapped claims tied to diagnosis R69 and temporary code groupings. Combined claim counts increased by more than 106,000 and unit cost signals also rose. Because the spend is unattributed and classification is weak, this is a validation queue first, not a clean clinical or authorization trend.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Unattributed temporary-code spend of this size can misdirect both utilization management and payment policy if it is treated as normal clinical growth.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Run a targeted data-quality and coding review on the UNATTRIBUTED OP HH/DME and OP Mgmt Oth Misc claims, focusing on R69 and temporary code buckets, then route only validated findings to clinical and UM teams.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The increase is concentrated in UNATTRIBUTED, Not Mapped, and temporary-code claims with repeated unmapped signals, so attribution and classification must be confirmed first.
evidence_summary: UNATTRIBUTED OP HH/DME added about +$33.4M on 42,681 more claims.
UNATTRIBUTED OP Mgmt Oth Misc added about +$22.6M on 63,836 more claims across temporary code buckets.
Both groups are concentrated in Not Mapped claims with diagnosis R69.
Combined unattributed impact is about +$55.9M.

business_patterns.top_pattern: IN DSNP HMO home health is showing real volume and cost pressure
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: IN DSNP HMO / HOME HEALTH - FREESTANDING
business_patterns.pattern_details: IN DSNP HMO home health at freestanding providers added about $7.1M and appears to reflect both more utilization and higher payment intensity. Unlike the larger IN Not Mapped issue, this pattern sits in a defined facility type and looks actionable. The business lever is home health authorization discipline, visit management, and contract review.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Home health growth can scale quickly in DSNP populations if visit controls and reimbursement terms are not aligned.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Launch an IN DSNP HMO home health action plan that audits top episodes and visit patterns, tightens prior authorization and continued-stay criteria, and checks paid rates against contract terms for freestanding home health.
evidence_summary: IN DSNP HMO home health added about +$7.1M.
Claims increased by 11,164.
The paid-per-admit or paid-per-claim signal increased by about $626.
The pattern is concentrated enough to support targeted UM and reimbursement action.

business_patterns.top_pattern: TX acute hospital spend is being driven by a handful of very high-cost IP Med/Surg cases
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: TX DSNP HMO / ACUTE HOSPITAL / IP Med/Surg
key_driver_codes: Disorders of Pancreas Except Malignancy with MCC
Lower Extremity and Humerus Procedures Except Hip, Foot, Femur with MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: TX DSNP HMO acute hospital spend is being pushed by a small set of very high-cost IP Med/Surg cases rather than broad-based utilization growth. The pattern centers on pancreatic disorders, pulmonary embolism, complex lower-extremity procedures, and inflammatory bowel disease, with several single-case increases near $0.2M. Some of the clinical records also show null or blank procedure fields, so case review and data validation should occur together.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Rare inpatient outliers need case-level intervention because the right lever may be catastrophic claim review, clinical management, payment integrity, or benefit design rather than broad utilization policy.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Open case-level review on the cited TX admissions, validate procedure completeness, and confirm whether outlier payment, case management, or acute inpatient authorization controls should be adjusted for these high-cost Med/Surg episodes.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The increase is concentrated in very small case counts and several clinical records contain null or blank procedure fields, so case details should be confirmed before policy action.
evidence_summary: TX IP Med/Surg rare-case groups total about +$1.9M when clinical and DSNP HMO acute hospital views are combined.
Key drivers include pulmonary embolism without MCC, pancreatic disorders with MCC, lower-extremity or humerus procedures with MCC, and inflammatory bowel disease with CC.
Several individual increases are about $0.2M on only 1 to 5 claims.
Clinical records include null or blank procedure fields.

business_patterns.top_pattern: OH DSNP HMO acute hospital pressure is concentrated in two hospitals
business_patterns.pattern_details: OH DSNP HMO acute hospital growth is concentrated at Kettering Health Dayton and Good Samaritan Hospital. Both providers show higher claim counts and higher paid per admit, pointing to targeted provider economics and utilization pressure instead of a broad statewide issue. This is a focused hospital action plan, not a systemwide trend.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: When cost growth is concentrated in a few hospitals, provider-specific contracting and admission management can produce faster savings than broad policy changes.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Run a provider-level contract and case-mix review for Kettering Health Dayton and Good Samaritan Hospital, paired with pre-service and continued-stay review on the affected acute admissions.
evidence_summary: OH DSNP HMO acute hospital increase totals about +$1.3M.
Kettering Health Dayton accounts for about +$740K on 662 more claims.
Good Samaritan Hospital adds about +$589K on 438 more claims.
Paid per admit rose by about $1.1K to $1.3K in the representative evidence.

business_patterns.top_pattern: CA acute hospital cost pressure is concentrated in a small provider and product mix
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA Medicare and DSNP products / ACUTE HOSPITAL

providers: EL CAMINO HEALTH - MOUNTAIN VIEW HOSPITAL

key_driver_codes: EL CAMINO HEALTH - MOUNTAIN VIEW HOSPITAL
Disorders of Pancreas Except Malignancy with MCC
Lower Extremity and Humerus Procedures Except Hip, Foot, Femur with MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: CA acute hospital pressure spans DSNP HMO, Medicare HMO, DSNP PPO, and CSNP PPO, with the largest concentration at El Camino Health - Mountain View Hospital and Good Samaritan Hospital. The increase reflects a mix of higher claim counts and elevated paid per admit in selected DRGs, especially chest procedures, pancreatic disorders, and lower-extremity or humerus procedures. This looks like concentrated provider and product mix pressure in acute settings.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A narrow set of hospitals and products creates a practical opportunity to renegotiate rates, steer volume, or tighten inpatient review without broad market disruption.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Perform hospital-by-hospital review of El Camino and Good Samaritan across the cited Medicare and DSNP products, comparing acute admission mix, paid rates, and steerage or UM opportunities.
evidence_summary: CA acute hospital pressure across DSNP and Medicare products totals about +$1.1M.
El Camino Health - Mountain View Hospital contributes about +$642K.
Major Chest Procedures with CC, pancreatic disorders with MCC, and lower-extremity or humerus procedures with MCC are recurring drivers.
There is also a smaller volume-led increase of about +$87K in CA DSNP HMO acute hospital claims.

business_patterns.top_pattern: OH transportation-related claims are rising in Not Mapped buckets around one provider
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: OH Medicare HMO and DSNP HMO / Not Mapped transportation-related claims
business_patterns.pattern_details: OH shows repeated growth in Not Mapped transportation-related claims tied to Midwest Medical Transport Company across both Medicare HMO and DSNP HMO. The same provider also appears in outpatient management categories under transportation services including ambulance. Because these claims are both concentrated and not well classified, validation of mapping and authorization edits should happen before the trend is treated as normal utilization.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Transportation spend can expand quickly through coding, routing, or authorization gaps, and a single-provider concentration makes this highly actionable.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Audit Midwest Medical Transport Company claims in OH for facility mapping, transport classification, and prior authorization or edit compliance, then decide whether the increase reflects valid transport utilization or preventable leakage.
business_patterns.validation_reason: All contributing groups are tied to Not Mapped or unmapped-value signals, and the pattern is concentrated at one transportation provider across products.
evidence_summary: OH not-mapped transportation-related claims total about +$576K across Medicare HMO and DSNP HMO.
MIDWEST MEDICAL TRANSPORT COMPANY drives the operational increases: about +$268K in Medicare HMO and +$203K in DSNP HMO.
Clinical transportation-related outpatient patterns add another about +$105K across R404, R0602, and R2689.
All contributing groups carry Not Mapped or unmapped-value signals.

business_patterns.top_pattern: CA outpatient oncology spend rose in a small number of chemotherapy claims
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA OP IV Thrpy/Oncology / Chemotherapy Drugs

providers: EL CAMINO HEALTH - MOUNTAIN VIEW HOSPITAL

key_driver_codes: EL CAMINO HEALTH - MOUNTAIN VIEW HOSPITAL
business_patterns.pattern_details: CA outpatient IV therapy and oncology spend increased in a small number of chemotherapy drug claims at Good Samaritan Hospital and El Camino Health - Mountain View Hospital. The increase is tied to diagnoses Z5111 and C180 inside a Not Mapped grouping, suggesting either a narrow oncology mix shift or incomplete classification. Oncology case review and coding or payment validation should be coordinated before broader policy changes.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Oncology spend behaves differently from general outpatient growth, so small claim counts can still indicate meaningful gaps in regimen review, site-of-care strategy, or claim classification.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Review the underlying CA chemotherapy claims for regimen, place of service, and code mapping accuracy, then confirm whether current oncology authorization and payment rules match the observed utilization.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The pattern is low volume, concentrated in chemotherapy claims, and sits in a Not Mapped grouping, so coding and classification should be confirmed before action.
evidence_summary: CA outpatient IV therapy or oncology adds about +$153K.
GOOD SAMARITAN HOSPITAL contributes about +$118K across 21 more chemotherapy drug claims.
EL CAMINO HEALTH - MOUNTAIN VIEW HOSPITAL contributes about +$35K.
Both drivers sit in a Not Mapped grouping with diagnoses Z5111 and C180.

executive_summary.headline: The dominant story is unresolved classification in IN and UNATTRIBUTED spend, followed by concentrated DSNP and Medicare hospital or home health pressure at a small number of providers.
executive_summary.primary_business_message: Two validation issues account for most of the observed increase: the IN DSNP HMO Not Mapped bucket and UNATTRIBUTED outpatient temporary-code spend. Outside those gating issues, the most actionable patterns are IN home health growth, concentrated acute hospital pressure in OH and CA, transportation-related Not Mapped claims in OH, and a small number of very high-cost TX inpatient Med/Surg cases.
recommended_focus_order: Validate the IN DSNP HMO and UNATTRIBUTED Not Mapped or temporary-code spend before changing authorization or network policy.
Address concentrated provider and site-of-care pressure in IN home health plus OH and CA acute hospitals.
Open case-level review for TX high-cost IP Med/Surg and CA outpatient oncology claims.
